Subject: Follow-up from today's call — Prod readiness constraints and SLOs

Thanks for the call this morning — good discussion. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions before we pull together a PoC scope: 

Top pain points (summary):
- Latency spikes affecting real-time triage UI during high traffic windows (peak 2–3pm PT).
- Cost unpredictability when synthetic traffic increases during batch jobs.
- Need for strong isolation for PHI-sensitive requests (SOC2 + custom retention).

Primary goals we agreed on:
- p95 inference latency <= 200ms for short classification prompts (~128 tokens).
- Sustainable baseline of 75 QPS with headroom for 200 QPS bursts for 10–15 minutes.
- End-to-end auditing and retention controls for deployed environments.

Clarifying questions for the Redwood team:
1) Which model variants do you recommend for mixed throughput/latency (generate vs classify)?
2) Can dedicated pools be pinned to a quantized variant for cost control, but automatically fallback to higher-precision if quality drops?
3) What telemetry will you expose for per-route token-level cost and KV-cache hit rates?

I've attached our initial requirements doc (medicore_poc_requirements.pdf). We'll need a short mutual action plan and a draft SOW to share with procurement.

Thanks,

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear summary and the requirements doc. Below is a concise post-call recap + recommended next steps from Redwood to shape the PoC and the MSA/procurement package.

Recap (we heard):
- Target p95 <= 200ms for classify/short prompts; acceptable p99 up to 400ms for long generating tasks.
- Baseline 75 QPS with burst to 200 QPS for 10–15 minutes; traffic pattern is bursty mid-day.
- PHI isolation + auditability are must-haves; encrypted payloads and audit logs required.

Redwood technical recommendations (PoC scope):
1) Deployment topology: Dedicated pool in us-west (customer VPC peering) with two variants: 
   - variant-a (high-precision): Llama2-Chat-70B fp16 on 4xA100-equivalent nodes for generate paths
   - variant-b (quantized): 8-bit quantized Llama2-70B / distilled 33B for classify paths — pinned to a reserved capacity plan to control spend
   - KV cache layer in front of both variants with prefix caching for repeat queries and a 128MB per-node cache target

2) Routing & fallbacks:
   - Smart routing policy: classify requests route to variant-b by default; generate requests route to variant-a.
   - Fallback flow: when variant-b experiences >5% quality regression (measured by evaluation set), automatically fail over to variant-a for that route.

3) Latency/throughput sizing:
   - Baseline: 6 nodes in the dedicated pool (target sustained 75 QPS).
   - Burst capacity: autoscale + warm standby (2 spare nodes) to reach 200 QPS within 90s.
   - Expected p95: ~120–180ms for classify on quantized variant at 75 QPS; ~220–350ms for generate on high-precision nodes depending on prompt length.

4) Observability & compliance:
   - Token-level cost, KV cache hit rate, per-route p95/p99, and per-request model variant logged to your S3 (or customer KMS-backed bucket).
   - SOC2 artifacts & a compliance checklist will be provided; retention controls configurable per-route (30/90/365 days).

5) Security:
   - Private deployment option (VPC peering) for the PoC.
   - Optional HSM-backed key wrap for payloads.

Next steps & asks from Medicore:
- Confirm which two representative routes we should include in the PoC (example: "triage-classify", "note-generation").
- Share a 1-week sample of traffic shape (hourly QPS) and a small eval set for quality checks.
- Procurement: point contact and suggested timeline for a short MSA + 3-month reserved capacity pilot.

Action items (owner):
- Chloe: Draft PoC scope and cost estimate (by EOD Fri).
- Rishi: Provide topology diagram and autoscale plan (Monday).
- Medicore: Share eval set + traffic sample (Anna).

Attachments referenced: kv_cache_profile.csv (cache hit rate targets), redwood_poc-sla-template.docx (draft SLO template).

If this matches your understanding I'll convert this into a one-page mutual action plan and a draft SOW for procurement.

Best,
